verses.text: In the beginning the Word already existed. The Word was with God, and the Word was God.
He was with God in the beginning.
God made everything through him. Nothing that exists was made without him.
Life was in him, and that life was the light for all people.
The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has never overcome it.
God sent a man whose name was John.
He came to tell people about the light, so that everyone could believe because of what he said.
John himself was not the light. He came to tell people about the light.
The true light, who gives light to everyone, was coming into the world.
He was in the world, and the world was made through him, but the world did not recognise him.
He came to his own people, but his own people did not welcome him.
But to all who did welcome him, those who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God.
They became God's children, not by being born in the normal human way, not because of human desire or a husband's choice, but because God gave them new birth.
The Word became a human being and lived among us. We saw his glory, the glory of the only Son, who came from the Father. He was full of grace and truth.
John told people about him. He called out, "This is the one I was talking about when I said, 'The one who comes after me is greater than I am, because he existed before I was born.'"
From all that he has in full, we have all received one gift of grace after another.
The law was given through Moses, but grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
No one has ever seen God. But the only Son, who is close to the Father's heart, has shown us what God is like.
This is what John said when the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem sent priests and Levites to ask him, "Who are you?"
He did not refuse to answer. He told them plainly, "I am not the Christ, the Messiah."
They asked him, "Then who are you? Are you Elijah?" He said, "I am not." "Are you the Prophet we are expecting?" He answered, "No."
Then they said, "Tell us who you are, so that we can give an answer to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?"
John answered in the words of the prophet Isaiah: "I am the voice of someone shouting in the desert, 'Make a straight road for the Lord.'"
Some of the people who had been sent were Pharisees.
They asked him, "If you are not the Christ, or Elijah, or the Prophet, why are you baptising people?"
John answered, "I baptise with water. But someone is standing among you whom you do not know.
He is the one who comes after me, and he is greater than I am. I am not good enough even to untie the straps of his sandals."
All this happened at Bethany, on the other side of the Jordan River, where John was baptising.
The next day John saw Jesus coming towards him. He said, "Look! There is the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
This is the one I meant when I said, 'A man who comes after me is greater than I am, because he existed before I was born.'
I did not know who he was. But I came baptising with water so that he could be made known to the people of Israel."
Then John said, "I saw the Spirit come down from heaven like a dove and stay on him.
I still did not know who he was. But God, who sent me to baptise with water, told me, 'You will see the Spirit come down and stay on someone. He is the one who will baptise with the Holy Spirit.'
I have seen this happen, and I tell you that he is the Son of God."
The next day John was there again with two of his followers.
When he saw Jesus walking by, he said, "Look! There is the Lamb of God!"
When the two followers heard him say this, they went after Jesus.
Jesus turned round and saw them following him. He asked them, "What are you looking for?" They said, "Rabbi (which means Teacher), where are you staying?"
He replied, "Come and you will see." So they went and saw where he was staying, and they spent the rest of that day with him. It was about four o'clock in the afternoon.
One of the two men who heard what John said and then followed Jesus was Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter.
The first thing Andrew did was to find his brother Simon and tell him, "We have found the Messiah" (which means the Christ).
Then Andrew brought Simon to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, "You are Simon, the son of Jonah. But you will be called Cephas" (which means Peter, or "rock").
The next day Jesus decided to go to Galilee. He found Philip and said to him, "Follow me."
Philip came from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter.
Philip found Nathanael and told him, "We have found the one Moses wrote about in the Law, and the prophets also wrote about him. He is Jesus from Nazareth, the son of Joseph."
Nathanael asked, "Nazareth! Can anything good come from there?" Philip said, "Come and see."
When Jesus saw Nathanael coming towards him, he said about him, "Here is a true man of Israel. There is nothing false in him."
Nathanael asked, "How do you know me?" Jesus answered, "I saw you under the fig tree before Philip called you."
Then Nathanael said, "Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!"
Jesus said to him, "Do you believe just because I told you that I saw you under the fig tree? You will see much greater things than that."
Then he said, "I tell you for certain, you will see heaven open, and the angels of God going up and coming down on the Son of Man."
